# OpenVMM runtime: first release candidate

This release replaces QEMU with embedded OpenVMM and introduces native Linux
and Windows runtime packages. Both packages include the same Linux kernel and
initramfs, built once by the release workflow.

- Boot Linux directly without BIOS or UEFI firmware.
- Run the host runtime with KVM on Linux or Windows Hypervisor Platform (WHP)
  on Windows, without external VM or filesystem daemons.
- Replace the C guest agent with a single-threaded Rust agent using epoll and
  a framed, checksummed protocol over virtio-vsock.
- Share directories through virtio-fs with pinned host handles, blocked symlinks
  and reparse points, bounded requests, and guest-only permission changes.
- Drain stdout and stderr before reporting process completion.
- Build, test, and package with mise; provide a static Linux musl runtime and
  a Windows MSVC runtime, plus a Debian package.

## Compatibility and validation

Temporary storage now uses raw disk images instead of qcow2; existing temporary
qcow2 data is not compatible. GPU passthrough is outside this release's scope.

Linux CI validates real KVM boots, networking, volumes, shared files, process
output, and shutdown. Windows CI validates native tests, builds, and packaging;
VM boot through WHP still requires validation on a Windows host with WHP enabled.
